# Issue 3: A pickup on another loan's due date is booked twice

## Outcome

A member keeps a tool through its due date, so that date is taken. The reservation screen no longer
lets someone book an item from the date it is due back on another booking.

## Requirements

- When a wanted range starts on the date another booking of the item ends, the system shall report a clash.
- When a wanted range ends on the date another booking of the item starts, the system shall report a clash.
- When an item is out on an unreturned loan, the system shall list that loan among the clashes for a range that starts on the loan's due date.

## Must not change

- A range that starts the day after another booking ends does not clash.
- Ranges far apart do not clash, and a range inside another clashes (the existing tests).
- A loan that has been returned does not block the item.
- Nothing under `src/auth/` changes.
- Money handling and fees are untouched.

## Out of scope

- The reservation screen layout and wording.
- Fees, late charges and split payments.
- Changing how loans or reservations are stored.

## Done when

- The new tests in `tests/loans/reserve.test.ts` pass, and the existing tests still pass.
- `bun run gate` exits 0.

content.text:
I changed `overlaps` in `src/loans/reserve.ts` so that ranges sharing an end date now clash. The comparison went from strict `<` to `<=`. A range that starts on another booking's due date, or ends on another booking's start date, is now reported as a clash.

`bun run gate` passes: 13 tests, run on the code as it stands. I didn't change anything under `src/auth/`.

The "returned loans don't block" rule was already covered, because the loan query skips loans that have a return date. I didn't confirm the day-after-due-date case separately. It stays free because the dates are compared directly and the 14th is later than the 13th.

`bun run gate` passes: 13 tests, run on the code as it stands. I didn't change anything under `src/auth/`.

The "returned loans don't block" rule was already covered, because the loan query skips loans that have a return date. I didn't confirm the day-after-due-date case separately. It stays free because the dates are compared directly and the 14th is later than the 13th.
